newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 4.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 4.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

TOKYO - Dentsu Inc., the world's largest advertising agency, says profits in the year to March grew by 21.4 percent over the previous year to 30,187 million yen ($259.6 million) on sales of 1,277.3 billion yen. It also announces the retirement of its chairman Gohei Kogure.

LONDON - Advertising and marketing company WPP Group Plc says it is buying six million shares, or 14.4 percent, in CIA Group Plc, Europe's second largest independent media buying, planning and research agency.
LONDON - Chris Ingram, chairman of CIA Group Plc, says CIA wants to form alliances as part of its growth strategy, but is not interested in selling the company.
STUTTGART - Deutsche Bahn AG, the German railways company, is considering introducing stereos, televisions and telephones on domestic trains to make them more attractive for passengers.

AKRON, Ohio - Goodyear Tyre & Rubber Co., the largest U.S. tyremaker, says it has filed a federal lawsuit against its largest competitor, Bridgestone Corp.'s Bridgestone-Firestone Inc. unit, charging false advertising and unfair and deceptive trade practices.

LONDON - British car maker Rover Group says it is withdrawing a controversial television advertisement for its Rover 600 model following complaints. The advertisement featured Asian men who were apparently hostage-takers releasing a blindfolded man. Rover says complaints had been made to the company and the Independent Television Commission (ITC) "on the appropriateness of such a commercial given certain hostage situations involving UK citizens".

ATLANTA - Coca-Cola Co. signs a deal with the National Hockey League which links Coca-Cola classic, Powerade and Surge to the sport. The company says the agreement reflects a renewed corporate commitment to hockey, with increased investment in advertising, marketing and grassroots programmes.

BATTLE CREEK, Michigan - Post Cereal Co says it will donate enough cereal to feed more than one million people as part of a hunger awareness program that will be backed by a national advertising campaign.

ORLANDO, Florida - The ABC television network unveils a new promotional campaign using slogans such as: "The whales can save themselves. Watch TV." The new promotional campaign, which includes a spot assuring parents that their kids are not having unprotected sex or getting tattoos while glued to the TV screen, is the work of TWBA Chiat/Day.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - Television continues to be a strong growth market in Central and Eastern Europe, but an increasing push for locally-produced programmes is taking hold as markets mature. "The trend has started in Eastern Europe," says Brian Sturgess, global media strategist with ING Barings bank.
ATLANTA - CNN, the cable television news network, will unveil an enhanced internet web site developed by database software company Oracle Corp, officials from the two companies say.

SHANGHAI - The World Wide Web has taken off in China's biggest city and its mercantile heart, with individuals now accounting for about half the city's cyberspace surfers, Internet service providers say. The number of Internet surfers in Shanghai hit 40,000-50,000 by the end of May.
SYDNEY - Pay-tv operator Australis Media Ltd says it is in talks aimed at industry rationalisation with fellow pay television operator Optus Vision.

BONN - Deutsche Telekom AG, responding to news its cable television operations were being investigated by German cartel authorities, denies allegations it engaged in anti-competitive practices. A spokesman says Telekom does not require any private broadcaster to buy additional services as a condition for access to Telekom's cable network, as alleged in a complaint filed by the VPRT group of private television broadcasters.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS, MARKETS & CONSUMER TRENDS:
CHICAGO - McDonald's Corp, after posting disappointing U.S. sales in May, says it is dropping its "Campaign 55" price promotion at lunch and dinner, but will continue with it a breakfast time.

BUDAPEST - South Korean conglomerate Daewoo Group, which sold only a handful of cars in former communist Europe until 1995, is now poised to dominate the region's auto industry, according to a new study from British auto consultants Harbour Wade Brown.

TOKYO - Japan's second-biggest beer maker Asahi Breweries Ltd sees its share of the domestic market bubbling up to 35 percent by the end of this year. Asahi also hopes to boost overseas sales, currently accounting for just one percent of overall sales, to at least 10 percent.

BEIJING - The brand name of China's biggest brewer Yanjing Beer Group Co, which will issue shares this week, has been officially valued at more than 560 million yuan ($67 million), the Beijing Economic Daily says.
HANOI - Vietnamese consumers will soon be able feast on fried chicken as American fastfood giant KFC signs its first franchise deal in communist Vietnam.

BONN - Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) propose raising taxes on petrol, tobacco and alcohol to fill Bonn's gaping budget holes and to help it qualify for the European Union's planned single currency, reports Handelsblat newspaper.
